history.summary: A well-built Wheelock-developed 1,012 sqft 3BR in Ang Mo Kio, 430m from Mayflower TEL station, asking $2,075 PSF — fractionally below the project's $2,101 URA median. Backed by a strong 6.1% resale CAGR over 195 transactions and a high liquidity profile (698 units, deep data), this is a solid, well-priced D20 buy with the main caveats being efficient-but-tight unit size and some early ageing of communal areas.

Reputable developer (Wheelock) with generally good build feedback. Score 738 / MMR 1539, on the frontier. Tempered from Strong Buy by reports that communal/roof facilities are ageing faster than expected and occasional lift/utility complaints, the relatively compact 1,012 sqft for a 3BR, and a 99yr lease (from 2013) that is fine now but not a freehold scarcity play.

history.summary: A 1,012 sqft 3BR at The Panorama (D20/OCR, Ang Mo Kio Ave 2, 698 units, TOP 2017, 86yrs lease left) asking $2.00M / $1,976 psf after a $2.10M -> $2.00M cut. The development itself is genuinely sound — 296 of 296 recorded resale exits profitable (REALSCORE 4.3), 979 transactions, 50+ deals a year, 272m to Mayflower TEL and 117m to CHIJ St Nicholas Girls'. But the entry edge is thinner than the headline: against the project's own same-size (1,011.82 sqft) prints the ask is -3.5% on 24 months and -8.9% on 12, and the project's size-controlled appreciation has decelerated to ~2.3-3.3%/yr, not the 6.07% trailing CAGR the ROI model runs on. Re-priced at a defensible 3.5%/yr the all-cash return is ~3.5-3.7%/yr on 1.84% net carry, into a ~4,200-unit Lentor supply wave landing inside the hold window. Good project, fair-to-slightly-cheap price — a hold, not an edge.
history.rating_rationale: Neutral because the quality is real but the mispricing is not large enough to pay for the headwinds. The bull case is downside protection, not upside: 296/296 profitable exits over a 6.7yr average hold with $126M of realized profit is the deepest clean profitability record I have seen on this book, and it is backed by 698 units, 979 transactions and a top-tier girls' school 117m away — this project does not lose owners money. The bear case is that everything driving the 757 score is backward-looking. The single largest MMR component is appreciation (+6.2) sourced from a 6.07% trailing 5yr CAGR, which our own backtest gives ~0 forward power; controlling for size, the 960-1060 sqft band went $1,930 psf (2023) -> $2,032 (2024) -> $2,088 (2025) -> $2,127 (2026), i.e. +3.3%/yr over three years and +2.3%/yr over two. Re-scored at 3.5%/yr the all-cash ROI falls from 5.79% to 3.52% annualized. The value signal — the one thing that does predict forward returns — is only -2.0% vs age-adjusted D20 peers and -3.5% vs same-size 24mo prints; the flattering -8.9% is against just six 12mo prints spanning $1,927-$2,253 psf, a 17% dispersion that does not track floor level, so it is as much noise as discount. A same-size mid-floor unit printed $1,927 psf in Jan-26, below this ask. Against that, ~4,200-4,390 new units TOP within 2km through 2027-2030 (Lentor planning-area vacancy already 7-9% vs 5-6% islandwide), OCR non-landed slipped -0.2% in Q2 2026, and net yield is 1.84% — negative carry for any leveraged buyer. Cheapest live 1,012 sqft ask by 9% and a motivated seller keep this off Avoid; a thin, floor-unverified discount into a supply wave keep it off Buy. Medium confidence: the project-level facts are decisive and well-evidenced, but floor, stack and facing are unverifiable and the forward call rests on supply/macro direction rather than certainty.
red_flags: Score is carried by a stale trailing CAGR: appreciation (+6.2) is the largest single MMR component and comes from a 6.07%/yr 5yr URA CAGR that is inflated by the 2021-23 surge (960-1060 sqft band: $1,626 psf 2021 -> $1,808 2022 -> $1,930 2023). Size-controlled, the last 3yrs run +3.3%/yr and the last 2yrs +2.3%/yr; re-scored at 3.5% the all-cash ROI drops 5.79% -> 3.52% annualized

Value edge is modest once the right comp is used: -2.0% vs age-adjusted D20 peers, -4.1% vs project URA median, -3.5% vs same-size 24mo prints. Only the 12mo same-size window gives -8.9%, and that is 6 prints spanning $1,927-$2,253 psf

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Adequate but thin and about to face competition. Realsmart logs 65 rental contracts in the past month across 698 units at $5.67 avg psf and a 3.2% estimated project yield; a 3BR of 1,100-1,200 sqft leased at $5,200 in Jun-26, so $4,800-5,000 is the realistic band for this 1,012 sqft unit and the model's $5,000 sits at the top of it. That produces 3.0% gross / 1.84% net — carry, not a yield play, and negative carry on leverage. Demand fundamentals are sound (TEL one-stop access, CHIJ St Nicholas catchment, AMK/Bishan employment and tuition belt) but the near-term direction is down: suburban rents are forecast to soften on supply, Lentor planning-area vacancy is running 7-9% against 5-6% islandwide, and ~4,200 units TOP in the precinct over 2026-27. A landlord here is one of many competing with an identical 3BR layout.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Materially weaker than the data rate implies, and I am overriding it. The 6.07% trailing 5yr CAGR is a real number but it is a regime artifact: size-controlled on the 960-1060 sqft band, median PSF ran $1,626 (2021) -> $1,808 (2022) -> $1,930 (2023) -> $2,032 (2024) -> $2,088 (2025) -> $2,127 (2026). The surge is 2021-23; the last three years annualize to +3.3%/yr and the last two to +2.3%/yr. Realsmart's own series agrees (2023 $1,887 -> 2026 $2,104 = +3.7%/yr) and momentum is already negative at -0.427. Forward, I use 3.5%/yr: the midpoint of the project's decelerating 2.3-3.3% size-controlled run-rate and the OCR realized-forward baseline of 3.7%, consistent with agency 2026 forecasts of 2-4.5% and with OCR non-landed printing -0.2% in Q2 2026. The Lentor supply wave is a specific dated drag on the back half of the hold; the offset is that new stock clears at $2,100-2,700 psf and re-anchors the catchment above this ask. At 3.5% the all-cash return is 3.52%/yr (5yr) and 3.69%/yr (7yr) — acceptable, unexciting, and not worth a Buy.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: Unverifiable — this is the main evidence gap. No profiles/ entry exists for The Panorama (stack_profile status 'not_researched') and neither the listing nor the DB record carries a floor, stack or facing; the address resolves only to block 8 Ang Mo Kio Ave 2, one of six towers (two 20-storey, four 17-storey) across 8/10/12/16/18/20. The usual test — does the ask sit below the stack's own prints because it is a low floor — does not resolve here, because at this project floor level does not explain price: within the exact 1,011.82 sqft cohort, a 01-05 floor unit printed $2,213 psf in Apr-26 while an 11-15 floor unit printed $1,927 psf in Jan-26, and a 01-05 printed $2,041 psf in May-26. Dispersion is condition-, renovation- and urgency-driven rather than positional, so the $1,976 ask can be neither credited as a positional bargain nor dismissed as a floor artifact.
